title: Network & Web Security
description: Learn how networks and websites are protected, explore common web vulnerabilities, and understand the security mechanisms used to prevent attacks.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a Network Firewall?
options: To monitor and filter incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predetermined security rules
To physically extinguish electrical fires inside server racks
To accelerate download speeds by 500%
To convert analog audio into digital music

explanation.asking: This question tests the foundational role of a network firewall.
explanation.why_correct: A firewall is a network security device that monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic based on an organization's previously established security policies, acting as a barrier between trusted and untrusted networks.

options_breakdown.To monitor and filter incoming and outgo: Correct. Firewalls enforce access control policies across network boundaries.
options_breakdown.To physically extinguish electrical fire: Incorrect. Fire suppression systems extinguish physical fires; cyber firewalls filter digital packets.
options_breakdown.To accelerate download speeds by 500%: Incorrect. Firewalls inspect packets and do not artificially increase ISP bandwidth.
options_breakdown.To convert analog audio into digital mus: Incorrect. Audio converters handle sound, not network packet security.

explanation.key_term: Firewall: A network security system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predetermined security rules.

questions.question: What is the key difference between an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) and an Intrusion Prevention System (IPS)?
options: An IDS monitors and alerts on detected suspicious traffic; an IPS actively blocks or drops malicious traffic in real time
An IDS is hardware, while an IPS is only software
An IDS only runs on smartphones, while an IPS only runs on routers
There is zero difference; both are identical acronyms

explanation.asking: This question asks about the operational distinction between passive detection (IDS) and active prevention (IPS).
explanation.why_correct: An IDS is a passive listening system that analyzes traffic copies and raises alerts when threats are identified. An IPS sits inline in the direct traffic path and actively drops or blocks malicious packets in real time.

options_breakdown.An IDS monitors and alerts on detected s: Correct. IDS alerts; IPS actively blocks threats inline.
options_breakdown.An IDS is hardware, while an IPS is only: Incorrect. Both can be deployed as dedicated hardware appliances or virtual software sensors.
options_breakdown.An IDS only runs on smartphones, while a: Incorrect. Both protect enterprise networks, servers, and cloud environments.
options_breakdown.There is zero difference; both are ident: Incorrect. Detection and prevention represent distinct operational modes.

explanation.key_term: IDS vs IPS: An IDS detects and alerts on malicious activity passively; an IPS actively takes automated inline action to prevent or block the activity.

questions.question: What does a Virtual Private Network (VPN) do when you connect to the Internet?
options: It creates an encrypted secure tunnel between your device and a remote VPN server, shielding your traffic and hiding your real IP address from local snoops
It provides unlimited free satellite electricity to your laptop battery
It deletes all your browsing history from every computer in the world
It makes your computer completely immune to all software bugs

explanation.asking: This question tests understanding of the core purpose of a VPN.
explanation.why_correct: A VPN encrypts internet traffic from the client device to the VPN gateway. This protects sensitive data from interception on untrusted local networks (like public coffee shop Wi-Fi) and masks the user's true geographic IP address.

options_breakdown.It creates an encrypted secure tunnel be: Correct. VPNs provide encryption and endpoint privacy across public networks.
options_breakdown.It provides unlimited free satellite ele: Incorrect. VPNs are software networking tools and cannot supply electrical power.
options_breakdown.It deletes all your browsing history fro: Incorrect. VPNs encrypt network transit; they do not erase server-side database logs.
options_breakdown.It makes your computer completely immune: Incorrect. VPNs do not patch software vulnerabilities or stop malware execution.

explanation.key_term: VPN (Virtual Private Network): An encrypted connection over the Internet from a device to a network that helps ensure sensitive data is safely transmitted.

questions.question: Why is HTTPS preferred over plain HTTP for web browsing?
options: HTTPS encrypts all transmitted data (including passwords and session cookies) using TLS, protecting it from eavesdropping and tampering
HTTPS makes websites load with larger fonts and brighter colors
HTTPS requires users to pay an annual subscription fee to the web designer
HTTPS is an operating system developed by Microsoft

explanation.asking: This question tests the security benefits of HTTPS over plain text HTTP.
explanation.why_correct: HTTP transmits web traffic in plain text, allowing anyone on the network to intercept credentials and sensitive data. HTTPS wraps HTTP inside Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption, ensuring confidentiality and integrity.

options_breakdown.HTTPS encrypts all transmitted data (inc: Correct. HTTPS provides confidentiality, data integrity, and server authentication.
options_breakdown.HTTPS makes websites load with larger fo: Incorrect. CSS styles fonts and colors, not transport security protocols.
options_breakdown.HTTPS requires users to pay an annual su: Incorrect. HTTPS is an open, free security protocol.
options_breakdown.HTTPS is an operating system developed b: Incorrect. HTTPS is an application-layer network protocol, not an operating system.

explanation.key_term: HTTPS: An extension of the Hypertext Transfer Protocol that uses encryption for secure communication over a computer network.

questions.question: What is 'SQL Injection' (SQLi)?
options: An attack where malicious SQL database statements are inserted into user entry fields (like login forms or search boxes) to manipulate the backend database
Injecting medicine into a computer processor with a syringe
Physically drilling a hole into the server hard drive
An attack that forces a computer to play audio at maximum volume

explanation.asking: This question asks for the definition of SQL injection.
explanation.why_correct: SQL injection occurs when untrusted user input is concatenated directly into a SQL query without proper sanitization or parameterization, allowing an attacker to bypass authentication, dump tables, or modify database data.

options_breakdown.An attack where malicious SQL database s: Correct. SQLi manipulates application database queries through unescaped user input.
options_breakdown.Injecting medicine into a computer proce: Incorrect. In cybersecurity, 'injection' refers to code injection, not medical injections.
options_breakdown.Physically drilling a hole into the serv: Incorrect. SQL injection is an application-layer software attack.
options_breakdown.An attack that forces a computer to play: Incorrect. SQL injection targets relational database records, not speakers.

explanation.key_term: SQL Injection (SQLi): A code injection technique used to attack data-driven applications in which malicious SQL statements are inserted into an entry field for execution.

questions.question: What is 'Cross-Site Scripting' (XSS)?
options: A web vulnerability that enables attackers to inject malicious client-side scripts (such as JavaScript) into web pages viewed by other users
Writing code in two different programming languages simultaneously
Cross-country marathon running for computer scientists
A hardware fault that breaks the keyboard spacebar

explanation.asking: This question asks for the definition of Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
explanation.why_correct: XSS occurs when a web application includes unvalidated and unescaped user input in web pages sent to other users. The victim's browser executes the malicious script, allowing attackers to steal session cookies or deface pages.

options_breakdown.A web vulnerability that enables attacke: Correct. XSS executes unauthorized JavaScript within victim browser contexts.
options_breakdown.Writing code in two different programmin: Incorrect. That is polyglot programming, not XSS.
options_breakdown.Cross-country marathon running for compu: Incorrect. XSS is a software security flaw.
options_breakdown.A hardware fault that breaks the keyboar: Incorrect. XSS is a software vulnerability, not keyboard hardware damage.

explanation.key_term: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS): A type of security vulnerability typically found in web applications that enables attackers to inject client-side scripts into web pages viewed by other users.

questions.question: What is the 'OWASP Top 10'?
options: A globally recognized consensus document representing the top ten most critical web application security risks
The top 10 fastest computer processors on the commercial market
The top 10 best-selling cybersecurity video games
The top 10 richest cybersecurity software executives

explanation.asking: This question tests knowledge of the OWASP foundation and its flagship Top 10 project.
explanation.why_correct: The Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP) is a non-profit foundation. Its 'OWASP Top 10' is an authoritative awareness guide ranking the most prevalent and critical security risks in web applications (e.g., Broken Access Control, Injection, Cryptographic Failures).

options_breakdown.A globally recognized consensus document: Correct. The OWASP Top 10 standardizes awareness of the most critical web application flaws.
options_breakdown.The top 10 fastest computer processors o: Incorrect. OWASP is dedicated to software security, not hardware benchmarking.
options_breakdown.The top 10 best-selling cybersecurity vi: Incorrect. OWASP produces professional security documentation and tools.
options_breakdown.The top 10 richest cybersecurity softwar: Incorrect. OWASP is an open, non-profit security community.

explanation.key_term: OWASP Top 10: A regularly updated report outlining the most critical vulnerabilities currently affecting web applications.

questions.question: What does a locked padlock icon in your web browser's address bar indicate?
options: The connection between your browser and the website is encrypted using a valid TLS certificate issued by a trusted Certificate Authority
The website cannot be hacked by any cybercriminal in the world
The website is owned personally by the President or Prime Minister
Your computer screen is locked and cannot be turned off

explanation.asking: This question tests accurate understanding of browser security indicators (the TLS padlock).
explanation.why_correct: The padlock verifies that data in transit is encrypted using TLS and that the website's certificate was validated by a trusted CA. It does NOT guarantee that the site itself is safe from fraud, scams, or malicious intent.

options_breakdown.The connection between your browser and: Correct. The padlock indicates that transit communication is encrypted and the domain certificate is trusted.
options_breakdown.The website cannot be hacked by any cybe: Incorrect. Encrypted sites can still possess backend vulnerabilities or host scams.
options_breakdown.The website is owned personally by the P: Incorrect. Anyone can obtain a valid TLS certificate for their domain.
options_breakdown.Your computer screen is locked and canno: Incorrect. The browser icon has no relation to OS screen lock states.

explanation.key_term: Browser Padlock: An icon indicating that the connection to the web server is encrypted with TLS and authenticated with a valid digital certificate.

questions.question: What is the difference between a Stateless Packet-Filtering Firewall and a Stateful Inspection Firewall?
options: A stateless firewall inspects packets in isolation without context; a stateful firewall tracks active connection states (handshakes) and automatically permits established return traffic
A stateless firewall only works on federal holidays
A stateful firewall is made of concrete, while a stateless firewall is made of glass
Stateless firewalls only filter physical printer cables

explanation.asking: This question tests the core operational difference between stateless and stateful firewalls.
explanation.why_correct: Stateless firewalls filter each packet purely on static header fields (IP, port) without memory of prior packets. Stateful firewalls maintain a state table tracking active TCP/UDP sessions, allowing return traffic belonging to established connections automatically.

options_breakdown.A stateless firewall inspects packets in: Correct. Stateful firewalls track session state, making them far more secure and practical.
options_breakdown.A stateful firewall is made of concrete,: Incorrect. Firewalls are digital hardware appliances or software applications.
options_breakdown.Stateless firewalls only filter physical: Incorrect. Firewalls filter network layer packets, not printer hardware lines.

explanation.key_term: Stateful Firewall: A network firewall that tracks the operating state and characteristics of network connections traversing it.

questions.question: Which HTTP request method is used to submit sensitive data (such as login credentials or credit card forms) in the body of an HTTP request rather than in the URL query string?
options: POST
GET
HEAD
TRACE

explanation.asking: This question tests knowledge of HTTP methods for secure form submission.
explanation.why_correct: The POST method transmits form data inside the HTTP message body. The GET method appends parameters directly to the visible URL (e.g., ?password=123), which exposes sensitive credentials in browser history, bookmarks, and server access logs.

options_breakdown.POST: Correct. POST carries form parameters securely in the request body rather than exposing them in the URL.
options_breakdown.GET: Incorrect. GET appends parameters to the plaintext URL query string, exposing sensitive credentials in logs and history.
options_breakdown.HEAD: Incorrect. HEAD requests only the HTTP response headers without the message body.
options_breakdown.TRACE: Incorrect. TRACE performs a message loop-back test along the network path.

explanation.key_term: HTTP POST: An HTTP method designed to send data to the server to create or update resources, carrying data in the request body.

questions.question: What protocol deprecated and replaced the obsolete Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) protocol for modern web encryption?
options: Transport Layer Security (TLS)
Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP)
Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP)
Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP)

explanation.asking: This question tests protocol evolution history from SSL to TLS.
explanation.why_correct: SSL 1.0, 2.0, and 3.0 were deprecated due to severe cryptographic flaws (such as POODLE). Modern internet encryption relies on Transport Layer Security (TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3).

options_breakdown.Transport Layer Security (TLS): Correct. TLS is the modern cryptographic standard that replaced obsolete SSL.
options_breakdown.Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP): Incorrect. SMTP is an email transmission protocol.
options_breakdown.Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHC: Incorrect. DHCP automatically leases IP addresses.
options_breakdown.Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP): Incorrect. TFTP is a lightweight UDP file transfer tool.

explanation.key_term: TLS (Transport Layer Security): A cryptographic protocol designed to provide communications security over a computer network, succeeding SSL.

questions.scenario: An attacker enters the string "' OR '1'='1" into the password field of a vulnerable web login page.
questions.question: Why does this input trick the database into granting unauthorized administrative access?
options: It turns the SQL WHERE clause into a statement that is always mathematically TRUE, bypassing password verification
It turns off the electrical power to the database server
It changes the database language into ancient Latin
It formats the server hard drive and deletes all records

explanation.asking: This scenario tests understanding of classic SQL injection authentication bypass logic.
explanation.why_correct: The injected "' OR '1'='1" alters the SQL query logic: `WHERE username='admin' AND password='' OR '1'='1'`. Because '1'='1' is always true, the entire conditional evaluates to TRUE, bypassing authentication without knowing the password.

options_breakdown.It turns the SQL WHERE clause into a sta: Correct. Injecting a tautology ('1'='1') forces the SQL condition to always evaluate to TRUE.
options_breakdown.It turns off the electrical power to the: Incorrect. SQL text queries have no physical power disruption capability.
options_breakdown.It changes the database language into an: Incorrect. SQL injection manipulates query logic, not language translations.
options_breakdown.It formats the server hard drive and del: Incorrect. The injected payload executes an authentication query, not a DROP/format command.

explanation.key_term: Tautology Injection: A SQL injection technique that uses always-true conditional statements (like '1'='1') to bypass authentication.

questions.question: What is the role of an HTTP Cookie in modern web applications?
options: A small piece of data stored in the user's web browser that maintains session state and remembers login status across web requests
A baked chocolate dessert delivered to software engineers
A physical hardware chip soldered onto the computer motherboard
An antivirus scanner that removes computer viruses

explanation.asking: This question tests the definition and session management role of HTTP cookies.
explanation.why_correct: Because HTTP is a stateless protocol, servers issue an HTTP Cookie (containing a unique session ID) to the browser upon login. The browser automatically returns this cookie with every subsequent request to maintain the authenticated session.

options_breakdown.A small piece of data stored in the user: Correct. Cookies enable stateful authentication across stateless HTTP requests.
options_breakdown.A baked chocolate dessert delivered to s: Incorrect. While named after bakery cookies, in computing it is a data storage token.
options_breakdown.A physical hardware chip soldered onto t: Incorrect. Cookies are browser-stored text tokens, not physical hardware.
options_breakdown.An antivirus scanner that removes comput: Incorrect. Cookies store session data; they do not perform security scanning.

explanation.key_term: HTTP Cookie: A small block of data created by a web server while a user is browsing a website and placed on the user's computer by the user's web browser.

questions.question: Why is accessing sensitive accounts (like online banking) over unencrypted public coffee shop Wi-Fi without a VPN dangerous?
options: Anyone nearby on the same open wireless network can intercept unencrypted data packets or execute Man-in-the-Middle attacks
The coffee shop owner will automatically receive 50% of your bank account balance
Public Wi-Fi cables are physically too thin to carry bank passwords
Unencrypted Wi-Fi forces your laptop screen to invert its colors

explanation.asking: This question tests understanding of wireless eavesdropping risks on untrusted open networks.
explanation.why_correct: Open public Wi-Fi networks lack encryption between client devices and the access point. Anyone with packet sniffing software (like Wireshark) can capture transmitted unencrypted packets, session tokens, or spoof local traffic.

options_breakdown.Anyone nearby on the same open wireless: Correct. Open Wi-Fi exposes traffic to local packet sniffing and rogue access point interception.
options_breakdown.The coffee shop owner will automatically: Incorrect. Wireless signals do not automatically execute bank transfers to shop owners.
options_breakdown.Public Wi-Fi cables are physically too t: Incorrect. Wi-Fi uses radio waves, not physical cables, and bandwidth accommodates all text data.
options_breakdown.Unencrypted Wi-Fi forces your laptop scr: Incorrect. Open Wi-Fi has no effect on display color rendering.

explanation.key_term: Wi-Fi Eavesdropping: The unauthorized interception of network traffic transmitted across open or unencrypted wireless networks.

questions.scenario: A blog application allows users to submit comments without sanitizing HTML tags. An attacker posts a comment containing: `<script>alert('Hacked!');</script>`. Whenever any other user views the blog post, the popup alert box appears in their browser.
questions.question: What type of Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) is this?
options: Stored XSS (Persistent XSS)
Reflected XSS (Non-persistent)
DOM-based XSS
Buffer Overflow

explanation.asking: This scenario tests identification of Stored (Persistent) XSS.
explanation.why_correct: In Stored XSS, the malicious script is permanently stored in the application's backend database (e.g., in blog comments or user profiles). Every victim who visits the page retrieves and executes the malicious payload.

options_breakdown.Stored XSS (Persistent XSS): Correct. Stored XSS permanently embeds malicious script into the database, serving it to all subsequent page visitors.
options_breakdown.Reflected XSS (Non-persistent): Incorrect. Reflected XSS requires the victim to click a specially crafted link that immediately reflects the payload in a single response.
options_breakdown.DOM-based XSS: Incorrect. DOM XSS executes entirely within client-side JavaScript without necessarily storing payloads on the server.
options_breakdown.Buffer Overflow: Incorrect. Buffer overflow is a binary memory corruption vulnerability, not a web script injection flaw.

explanation.key_term: Stored XSS: A type of cross-site scripting where the malicious script is permanently stored on the target server (such as in a database) and served to users.

questions.question: What is the single most effective defensive programming technique to completely prevent SQL Injection vulnerabilities?
options: Using Parameterized Queries (Prepared Statements) with bound parameters
Hiding the database login page behind a dark background
Renaming the SQL database once every week
Turning off the monitor while running SQL queries

explanation.asking: This question asks for the primary, foolproof mitigation against SQL injection.
explanation.why_correct: Parameterized queries (Prepared Statements) separate SQL code from user data. The database treats user input strictly as literal parameter values, never as executable SQL commands, completely neutralizing injection attacks.

options_breakdown.Using Parameterized Queries (Prepared St: Correct. Prepared statements ensure user input can never alter query logic.
options_breakdown.Hiding the database login page behind a: Incorrect. Visual UI styling provides zero backend security against injection.
options_breakdown.Renaming the SQL database once every wee: Incorrect. Renaming tables disrupts operations and does not fix underlying SQL concatenation vulnerabilities.
options_breakdown.Turning off the monitor while running SQ: Incorrect. Turning off monitors has zero effect on backend software execution.

explanation.key_term: Prepared Statements: A feature used to execute the same or similar database statements repeatedly with high efficiency and complete protection against SQL injection.

questions.question: What is a 'Web Application Firewall' (WAF) and how does it differ from a standard network firewall?
options: A WAF operates at Layer 7 (Application layer) specifically inspecting HTTP/HTTPS traffic to block web attacks like SQLi and XSS; a network firewall operates at Layers 3/4 filtering IP addresses and ports
A WAF is only installed on smartphones, while a network firewall is installed in cars
A WAF deletes websites every midnight, while a network firewall keeps them online
There is zero difference; WAF is just an abbreviation for firewall

explanation.asking: This question tests the distinction between network firewalls (L3/L4) and web application firewalls (L7).
explanation.why_correct: Network firewalls filter based on IP addresses and TCP/UDP ports (Layers 3 and 4). A Web Application Firewall (WAF) operates at Layer 7, deeply inspecting HTTP request bodies and headers to detect application-layer attacks (SQLi, XSS, CSRF).

options_breakdown.A WAF operates at Layer 7 (Application l: Correct. WAFs inspect Layer 7 web payloads; network firewalls filter Layers 3 and 4.
options_breakdown.A WAF is only installed on smartphones,: Incorrect. Both protect enterprise servers, cloud clusters, and web applications.
options_breakdown.A WAF deletes websites every midnight, w: Incorrect. WAFs protect web applications from compromise.
options_breakdown.There is zero difference; WAF is just an: Incorrect. They operate at completely different OSI layers.

explanation.key_term: WAF (Web Application Firewall): A specific form of application firewall that filters, monitors, and blocks HTTP traffic to and from a web service.

questions.question: What is 'Private Browsing' or 'Incognito Mode' in web browsers, and what does it actually protect?
options: It prevents local browsing history, search records, and cookies from being saved to the local device after closing the window; it does NOT make you anonymous to your ISP or websites
It makes you 100% invisible to the police, government agencies, and internet providers
It automatically hacks into any Wi-Fi network nearby
It makes all websites on the Internet completely free of charge

explanation.asking: This question tests common misconceptions about Incognito / Private Browsing modes.
explanation.why_correct: Incognito mode only ensures that local session history, cache, and cookies are erased from the local computer when closed. It does NOT hide your traffic from your ISP, employer network filters, or the websites you visit.

options_breakdown.It prevents local browsing history, sear: Correct. Incognito protects local device privacy from peer users, not network anonymity.
options_breakdown.It makes you 100% invisible to the polic: Incorrect. ISPs, employers, and websites still see your IP address and visited domains.
options_breakdown.It automatically hacks into any Wi-Fi ne: Incorrect. Incognito is a local browser window setting, not a wireless cracking tool.
options_breakdown.It makes all websites on the Internet co: Incorrect. Browser privacy modes do not bypass commercial paywalls.

explanation.key_term: Incognito Mode: A privacy feature in some web browsers that prevents your browsing history from being stored locally on your device.

questions.question: What is the 'Same-Origin Policy' (SOP) enforced by modern web browsers?
options: A critical security mechanism that prevents JavaScript on one website from reading or accessing data and cookies on a completely different origin domain
A policy requiring all web servers to be manufactured in the same country
A rule that all employees must wear the same uniform when using web browsers
A policy requiring all web pages to have the same background color

explanation.asking: This question asks about the foundational web security sandbox: the Same-Origin Policy.
explanation.why_correct: The Same-Origin Policy (SOP) restricts how a document or script loaded by one origin (protocol + host + port) can interact with a resource from another origin, isolating malicious websites from reading your authenticated bank session.

options_breakdown.A critical security mechanism that preve: Correct. SOP isolates different web origins from accessing each other's private DOM and cookies.
options_breakdown.A policy requiring all web servers to be: Incorrect. SOP is a web browser software sandbox, not a hardware manufacturing rule.
options_breakdown.A rule that all employees must wear the: Incorrect. Workplace dress codes have no connection to web browser security policies.
options_breakdown.A policy requiring all web pages to have: Incorrect. Web designers have complete visual styling freedom.

explanation.key_term: Same-Origin Policy (SOP): A fundamental web application security model under which a web browser permits scripts contained in a first web page to access data in a second web page, but only if both web pages have the same origin.

questions.question: Which of the following actions promote safe and secure web browsing? (Select all that apply)
options: Verifying that websites use HTTPS before submitting passwords or personal info
Keeping your web browser and operating system updated with the latest security patches
Avoiding clicking suspicious links or downloading attachments from unknown senders
Typing your banking password into popup ads that claim your computer is infected

explanation.asking: This question asks you to identify safe web browsing best practices.
explanation.why_correct: Safe browsing includes verifying HTTPS, keeping browsers patched, and scrutinizing email links and attachments. Typing credentials into scareware popups directly causes account compromise.

options_breakdown.Verifying that websites use HTTPS before: Correct. HTTPS ensures sensitive communications are encrypted.
options_breakdown.Keeping your web browser and operating s: Correct. Patching eliminates vulnerabilities that enable drive-by downloads.
options_breakdown.Avoiding clicking suspicious links or do: Correct. Prudent caution stops phishing and malware infections.
options_breakdown.Typing your banking password into popup: Incorrect. This directly gives your credentials to cybercriminals running scareware scams.

explanation.key_term: Safe Browsing Practices: Habits and procedures users follow to protect their devices and data while navigating the internet.

questions.question: What is the difference between Reflected XSS and Stored XSS?
options: Reflected XSS reflects the malicious script immediately in the response from a single specially crafted link/request; Stored XSS saves the script permanently in the database to victimize any user visiting the page
Reflected XSS only works on mirrors, while Stored XSS works in grocery stores
Reflected XSS is hardware, while Stored XSS is software
There is zero difference; both are identical

explanation.asking: This question tests the distinction between Reflected (non-persistent) and Stored (persistent) XSS.
explanation.why_correct: Reflected XSS requires tricking a victim into clicking a link that embeds the payload into an immediate server response (e.g., search error message). Stored XSS injects the payload into the database, serving it automatically to every future visitor.

options_breakdown.Reflected XSS reflects the malicious scr: Correct. Reflected requires individual victim link delivery; Stored persists in the database.
options_breakdown.Reflected XSS only works on mirrors, whi: Incorrect. These are word puns, not web security concepts.
options_breakdown.Reflected XSS is hardware, while Stored: Incorrect. Both are software web application injection vulnerabilities.
options_breakdown.There is zero difference; both are ident: Incorrect. They have fundamentally different persistence and delivery mechanics.

explanation.key_term: Reflected XSS: A non-persistent cross-site scripting attack where the injected script is reflected off the web server in an error message, search result, or response.

questions.scenario: A bank customer logs into their online banking account. In another browser tab, they visit a malicious site that contains a hidden image tag: ``. The browser automatically sends the user's active session cookie, executing the unauthorized transfer.
questions.question: What attack technique did the customer suffer?
options: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
SQL Injection
Buffer Overflow
Denial of Service

explanation.asking: This scenario tests understanding of Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF).
explanation.why_correct: CSRF tricks an authenticated victim's browser into transmitting unauthorized state-changing HTTP requests to a vulnerable application that implicitly trusts the user's automatic session cookies.

options_breakdown.Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF): Correct. CSRF exploits ambient cookie authentication to execute actions on behalf of authenticated users.
options_breakdown.SQL Injection: Incorrect. SQL injection manipulates backend database SQL queries.
options_breakdown.Buffer Overflow: Incorrect. Buffer overflow is a memory corruption exploit.
options_breakdown.Denial of Service: Incorrect. DoS disrupts availability, whereas CSRF forged an authenticated transaction.

explanation.key_term: CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery): An attack that forces an end user to execute unwanted actions on a web application in which they are currently authenticated.

questions.question: How do modern web applications defend against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks?
options: By including unpredictable, cryptographically random Anti-CSRF Tokens in forms and verifying them on the server, and setting the 'SameSite=Strict' cookie attribute
By changing all passwords to lowercase letters
By turning off the web server whenever users log in
By removing all images from web pages

explanation.asking: This question asks about standard CSRF defense mechanisms.
explanation.why_correct: Anti-CSRF tokens (unique, secret values tied to the user session and validated on POST requests) and the 'SameSite' cookie attribute prevent external malicious origins from forging valid requests.

options_breakdown.By including unpredictable, cryptographi: Correct. Anti-CSRF tokens and SameSite cookies prevent cross-origin request forging.
options_breakdown.By changing all passwords to lowercase l: Incorrect. Weakening passwords harms security and does nothing to mitigate CSRF.
options_breakdown.By removing all images from web pages: Incorrect. CSRF can be triggered via forms, scripts, and fetch requests, not just images.

explanation.key_term: Anti-CSRF Token: A unique, unpredictable, and secret value generated by the server-side application and transmitted to the client in a way that is included in a subsequent HTTP request.

questions.scenario: A web developer adds the HTTP response header `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` to their web server configuration.
questions.question: What does the HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) header instruct browsers to do?
options: It forces browsers to only communicate with the website over secure HTTPS, automatically converting all unencrypted HTTP links and preventing SSL-stripping attacks
It forces users to change their password every 31,536,000 seconds
It locks the web server screen after 1 year of continuous operation
It deletes all emails sent to subdomains

explanation.asking: This scenario tests understanding of HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS).
explanation.why_correct: HSTS instructs browsers that a site must only be accessed over HTTPS for a specified duration (max-age). If an attacker tries to downgrade connections via an SSL-stripping attack, the browser blocks the connection.

options_breakdown.It forces browsers to only communicate w: Correct. HSTS enforces HTTPS and neutralizes SSL-stripping downgrade attacks.
options_breakdown.It forces users to change their password: Incorrect. HSTS governs transport protocol encryption, not user password expiration.
options_breakdown.It locks the web server screen after 1 y: Incorrect. HSTS is an HTTP header for web browsers, not an OS screen lock.
options_breakdown.It deletes all emails sent to subdomains: Incorrect. HSTS enforces web encryption across subdomains, not email deletion.

explanation.key_term: HSTS (HTTP Strict Transport Security): A web security policy mechanism that helps to protect websites against man-in-the-middle attacks such as protocol downgrade attacks and cookie hijacking.

questions.question: What does the `HttpOnly` flag on a session cookie protect against?
options: It prevents client-side JavaScript (document.cookie) from accessing or stealing the cookie during an XSS attack
It forces the website to run on port 80 without encryption
It deletes the cookie whenever the computer is restarted
It prevents users from taking screenshots of their computer monitor

options_breakdown.Replay Attack: Incorrect. Replay attacks retransmit captured valid authentication tokens.
options_breakdown.ARP Cache Poisoning: Incorrect. ARP poisoning corrupts Layer 2 switch forwarding tables.

explanation.key_term: WAF Evasion: Techniques used by attackers to disguise attack payloads so that a Web Application Firewall does not recognize the signature.

questions.scenario: A company decommissioned an AWS S3 bucket formerly used for `assets.company.com`, but left the DNS CNAME record pointing to the non-existent S3 bucket name in public DNS. An attacker creates an S3 bucket with that exact name and takes full control of `assets.company.com`, serving malicious JavaScript under the company's verified domain.
questions.question: What specific attack occurred?
options: Subdomain Takeover
SQL Injection
Clickjacking
Buffer Overflow

explanation.asking: This scenario tests understanding of Subdomain Takeovers via dangling DNS records.
explanation.why_correct: Subdomain Takeover occurs when a DNS record (like a CNAME) points to an external cloud resource (AWS S3, GitHub Pages, Heroku) that has been deleted or unclaimed. Attackers claim the resource name and gain full control over the corporate subdomain.

options_breakdown.Subdomain Takeover: Correct. Claiming dangling cloud resources mapped by DNS CNAME records achieves Subdomain Takeover.
options_breakdown.SQL Injection: Incorrect. SQL injection targets application databases.
options_breakdown.Clickjacking: Incorrect. Clickjacking overlays transparent iframes on web buttons.
options_breakdown.Buffer Overflow: Incorrect. Buffer overflow corrupts application memory stacks.

explanation.key_term: Subdomain Takeover: A process where an attacker gains control over a subdomain of a target domain by pointing to an unclaimed third-party cloud service.

questions.scenario: A mobile security analyst tests an iOS banking application and observes that the application refuses to establish HTTPS connections when routed through Burp Suite with a custom CA root certificate installed on the device.
questions.question: Which defensive mechanism implemented in the mobile app's code is blocking the intercepting proxy?
options: SSL / TLS Certificate Pinning
HSTS Header enforcement alone
Cross-Origin Resource Sharing
Operating System Defragmentation

explanation.asking: This scenario tests identification of SSL/TLS Certificate Pinning in mobile security assessments.
explanation.why_correct: Mobile applications implement SSL Pinning by hardcoding expected public key hashes directly into application binaries. Even if an analyst installs a trusted CA onto the test device, the pinned app rejects the proxy certificate because its key doesn't match the pinned hash.

options_breakdown.SSL / TLS Certificate Pinning: Correct. Certificate pinning blocks intercepting proxies by requiring exact cryptographic key matches hardcoded in the app.
options_breakdown.HSTS Header enforcement alone: Incorrect. HSTS forces HTTPS, but trusts any valid CA installed in the system trust store.
options_breakdown.Cross-Origin Resource Sharing: Incorrect. CORS is a browser cross-origin policy, not a mobile network socket control.
options_breakdown.Operating System Defragmentation: Incorrect. Defragmentation arranges disk blocks on spinning hard drives.

explanation.key_term: SSL Pinning: The practice of hardcoding the server's certificate or public key within a client application to prevent MitM attacks using forged or custom root CAs.

questions.scenario: An application deserializes untrusted user-supplied JSON or Python pickle objects directly using `pickle.loads(user_input)` without sanitization.
questions.question: What critical vulnerability allows an attacker to construct a serialized object that executes arbitrary operating system commands during deserialization?
options: Insecure Deserialization
SQL Injection
Clickjacking
Reflected XSS

explanation.asking: This scenario tests understanding of Insecure Deserialization (OWASP Top 10).
explanation.why_correct: Insecure Deserialization occurs when untrusted data is used to instantiate objects in memory. In languages like Python, Java, or PHP, attackers craft malicious magic methods (`__reduce__`, `readObject`) that execute arbitrary shell commands upon deserialization.

options_breakdown.Insecure Deserialization: Correct. Deserializing untrusted object streams leads directly to Remote Code Execution (RCE).
options_breakdown.SQL Injection: Incorrect. SQL injection targets relational database queries.
options_breakdown.Reflected XSS: Incorrect. Reflected XSS executes JavaScript in victim web browsers.

explanation.key_term: Insecure Deserialization: A vulnerability where untrusted data is used to abuse the logic of an application, inflict a denial of service attack, or execute arbitrary code upon object deserialization.

questions.scenario: An attacker establishes a persistent two-way WebSocket connection to a financial application. By tricking a logged-in user into visiting a malicious site, the attacker initiates a WebSocket handshake from the malicious origin, exploiting the fact that WebSockets do not strictly enforce the Same-Origin Policy by default.
questions.question: What specific web attack is this?
options: Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH)
SQL Injection
Buffer Overflow
SYN Flooding

explanation.asking: This scenario tests knowledge of Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH).
explanation.why_correct: Unlike standard HTTP fetch requests constrained by SOP, the WebSocket specification does not enforce the Same-Origin Policy. Unless developers explicitly validate the `Origin` header during the initial HTTP Upgrade handshake, cross-site sites can hijack the connection.

options_breakdown.Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH): Correct. CSWSH abuses the lack of default SOP enforcement on WebSocket handshakes to steal live streaming data.
options_breakdown.SQL Injection: Incorrect. SQL injection manipulates SQL database syntax.
options_breakdown.Buffer Overflow: Incorrect. Buffer overflow corrupts application memory stacks.
options_breakdown.SYN Flooding: Incorrect. SYN flooding is a network transport exhaustion attack.

explanation.key_term: CSWSH: A cross-origin attack that exploits missing Origin validation during the WebSocket handshake to steal real-time bi-directional data.

questions.scenario: A web application uses a web template engine (such as Jinja2 in Python or Twig in PHP) and passes unsanitized user input directly into template string rendering: `render_template_string("Hello " + request.args.get('name'))`. An attacker submits `{{ 7 * 7 }}` and the screen renders `Hello 49`, followed by code that spawns an operating system shell.
questions.question: Which server-side template vulnerability did the attacker exploit to achieve remote arithmetic evaluation and shell execution?
options: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI)
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
SQL Injection
XML External Entity (XXE)

explanation.asking: This scenario tests identification of Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI).
explanation.why_correct: SSTI occurs when user input is concatenated directly into template engine directives rather than passed as data parameters. Attackers inject template syntax to access backend Python/PHP runtime objects and execute arbitrary code.

options_breakdown.Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI): Correct. SSTI abuses template engine syntax concatenation to achieve Remote Code Execution.
options_breakdown.Cross-Site Scripting (XSS): Incorrect. XSS executes in client browsers; SSTI evaluated arithmetic and code on the backend server.
options_breakdown.SQL Injection: Incorrect. SQL injection attacks relational database engines.

explanation.key_term: SSTI (Server-Side Template Injection): A vulnerability that occurs when an attacker is able to use native template syntax to inject a malicious payload into a template, which is then executed on the server.

questions.scenario: An attacker discovers that a web application uses a predictable, linear random number generator (such as standard `Math.random()` in JavaScript) to generate password reset tokens.
questions.question: Why is using standard pseudo-random number generators (PRNGs) cryptographically insecure for security tokens?
options: PRNGs are deterministic; an attacker who observes a sequence of outputs can mathematically calculate past and future generated tokens, predicting other users' password reset links
PRNGs physically overheat the computer processor
PRNGs only generate even numbers, never odd numbers
PRNGs automatically format the database server

explanation.asking: This scenario tests understanding of Cryptographically Secure Pseudo-Random Number Generators (CSPRNGs).
explanation.why_correct: Standard PRNGs (like linear congruential generators or Mersenne Twister) are designed for speed in simulations, not security. An observer can deduce the internal state from output samples. Security tokens require CSPRNGs (like `/dev/urandom` or `crypto.getRandomValues`).

options_breakdown.PRNGs are deterministic; an attacker who: Correct. Standard PRNGs leak internal state, allowing attackers to predict subsequent secret tokens.
options_breakdown.PRNGs physically overheat the computer p: Incorrect. PRNG calculations use minimal CPU cycles and have no severe thermal impact.
options_breakdown.PRNGs only generate even numbers, never: Incorrect. PRNGs produce uniform random distributions across odd and even integers.
options_breakdown.PRNGs automatically format the database: Incorrect. Number generators calculate mathematical values and do not execute disk commands.

explanation.key_term: CSPRNG: A pseudo-random number generator with properties that make it suitable for use in cryptography (unpredictability and forward/backward secrecy).

questions.scenario: An application uses a web form that executes a query against a PostgreSQL database. The application filters out single quotes (`'`) but fails to sanitize backslashes (`\`).
questions.question: How can an attacker use backslash characters to escape the SQL string literal and execute SQL injection?
options: The attacker injects a backslash `\` to escape the opening single quote in the application query, turning the subsequent SQL quote into data and escaping into raw SQL commands
The attacker types backslashes to physically reverse the direction of electrical current in the motherboard
The backslash deletes all tables in PostgreSQL automatically
The backslash forces PostgreSQL to convert into MySQL

explanation.asking: This scenario tests advanced SQL injection bypasses using backslash character escaping.
explanation.why_correct: If an application wraps input in `'` and escapes quotes by prepending `\'`, injecting a backslash results in `\'`. The injected backslash escapes the escape character, leaving the single quote intact to break out of the string literal.

options_breakdown.The attacker injects a backslash `\\` to: Correct. Backslash escaping bypasses naive quote filters by altering delimiter parsing.
options_breakdown.The attacker types backslashes to physic: Incorrect. SQL text characters have no electrical polarity reversal capability.
options_breakdown.The backslash deletes all tables in Post: Incorrect. A backslash is a literal character, not a destructive command.
options_breakdown.The backslash forces PostgreSQL to conve: Incorrect. Database software engines do not convert into competing products.

explanation.key_term: Character Escaping Bypasses: Techniques exploiting how backslashes and quote delimiters interact within database string parsers to break query boundaries.

questions.scenario: An API authentication service uses JSON Web Tokens (JWT). An attacker modifies the JWT header from `"alg": "RS256"` to `"alg": "none"` and strips the signature block entirely. The vulnerable backend accepts the token without verifying a signature, granting the attacker instant administrative access.
questions.question: What classic JWT vulnerability was exploited?
options: JWT 'none' Algorithm Vulnerability
SQL Injection
Buffer Overflow
Replay Attack

explanation.asking: This scenario tests understanding of the infamous JWT 'none' algorithm vulnerability (CVE-2015-9235).
explanation.why_correct: The JWT specification includes an algorithm `none` for unsecured tokens. Vulnerable JWT libraries accepted `"alg": "none"` without validating signatures, allowing attackers to forge arbitrary claims and tamper with tokens.

options_breakdown.JWT 'none' Algorithm Vulnerability: Correct. Flawed JWT implementations accepted 'none' algorithm headers, bypassing signature verification completely.
options_breakdown.SQL Injection: Incorrect. SQL injection targets relational database syntax.
options_breakdown.Buffer Overflow: Incorrect. Buffer overflow corrupts application memory stacks.
options_breakdown.Replay Attack: Incorrect. Replay attacks reuse unmodified authentic tokens; this forged arbitrary claims.

explanation.key_term: JWT 'none' Algorithm Flaw: A critical vulnerability where a server accepts JSON Web Tokens with the algorithm header set to 'none' without verifying any cryptographic signature.

questions.question: What is the security hazard of enabling `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on an internal enterprise API that requires user cookies for authentication?
options: Browsers strictly prohibit combining wildcard `*` with credentials (`Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`), but if an application dynamically reflects the request `Origin` header, any external website can steal authenticated private data
It causes all web servers in the world to immediately reboot
It uninstalls the web browser from the client's computer
It converts the user's hard drive into an optical laser disk

explanation.asking: This question tests CORS credential reflection vulnerabilities.
explanation.why_correct: The CORS standard explicitly forbids combining `Allow-Origin: *` with `Allow-Credentials: true`. However, vulnerable developers frequently bypass this error by dynamically echoing the incoming `Origin` header into `Allow-Origin`, opening authenticated endpoints to cross-origin data theft.

options_breakdown.Browsers strictly prohibit combining wil: Correct. Dynamic origin reflection with credentials bypasses SOP and leaks sensitive user data to malicious sites.
options_breakdown.It causes all web servers in the world t: Incorrect. CORS headers govern browser HTTP permissions, not server power management.
options_breakdown.It uninstalls the web browser from the c: Incorrect. CORS policies cannot execute OS uninstallations.
options_breakdown.It converts the user's hard drive into a: Incorrect. HTTP headers have no physical hardware transmutation properties.

explanation.key_term: CORS Origin Reflection: A common developer antipattern where the server dynamically echoes the client's Origin header into Access-Control-Allow-Origin, enabling credentialed cross-origin data theft.

questions.scenario: A banking web application generates session IDs using a 16-bit integer (supporting only 65,536 possible session IDs).
questions.question: Why does a small session ID entropy space leave the application vulnerable to session prediction attacks?
options: An attacker can easily brute-force and predict active session tokens within a few minutes using automated requests, hijacking live user sessions
It causes the web server's power supply to blow a fuse
It forces all customer accounts to change their names to 'Anonymous'
It prevents more than 16 users from using the website simultaneously

explanation.asking: This scenario tests session token entropy requirements (OWASP Session Management).
explanation.why_correct: Session identifiers must possess high cryptographic entropy (at least 128 bits of randomness). A 16-bit space has only 65,536 values, allowing an attacker to guess active tokens in seconds via automated brute force.

options_breakdown.An attacker can easily brute-force and p: Correct. Insufficient token entropy allows rapid guessing of active authenticated session IDs.
options_breakdown.It causes the web server's power supply: Incorrect. Session entropy is a cryptographic randomness metric, not an electrical power surge.
options_breakdown.It forces all customer accounts to chang: Incorrect. Token entropy does not alter database username fields.
options_breakdown.It prevents more than 16 users from usin: Incorrect. A 16-bit number supports up to 65,536 distinct integer values, not 16 users.

explanation.key_term: Session Token Entropy: A measure of the randomness and unpredictability of session identifiers, crucial for preventing session guessing attacks.

questions.scenario: An attacker positions themselves as a Man-in-the-Middle on an unencrypted Wi-Fi network and intercepts an initial plaintext HTTP request to `http://bank.com`. The attacker proxies the secure HTTPS connection to the bank, but strips all HTTPS links and forwards plain HTTP to the victim's browser.
questions.question: What classic protocol downgrade attack did the attacker execute (popularized by SSLstrip)?
options: SSL / TLS Stripping Attack
SQL Injection
Buffer Overflow
Clickjacking

explanation.asking: This scenario tests understanding of SSL Stripping attacks.
explanation.why_correct: In SSL Stripping, the attacker intercepts the client's initial unencrypted HTTP redirect, maintains an encrypted HTTPS session with the authentic server, but serves unencrypted HTTP back to the client, capturing plaintext credentials in transit. HSTS was created specifically to eliminate this attack.

options_breakdown.SSL / TLS Stripping Attack: Correct. SSL stripping downgrades HTTPS connections to unencrypted HTTP to intercept credentials in transit.
options_breakdown.SQL Injection: Incorrect. SQL injection manipulates relational database queries.
options_breakdown.Buffer Overflow: Incorrect. Buffer overflow corrupts application memory stacks.

explanation.key_term: SSL Stripping: A type of man-in-the-middle attack in which an attacker downgrades a secure HTTPS connection to an insecure HTTP connection.

questions.scenario: An engineer reviews an API and finds that an endpoint accepts JSON payloads: `{"user": "alice", "is_admin": false}`. When a regular user registers, they append `"is_admin": true` to the JSON body. Because the backend framework automatically binds all request properties directly to the User database model without filtering, the user is created as a full administrator.
questions.question: Which object-relational model binding vulnerability allowed the attacker to elevate their account privileges to administrator?
options: Mass Assignment (Over-Posting / Auto-Binding Vulnerability)
SQL Injection
Cross-Site Scripting
XML External Entity (XXE)

explanation.asking: This scenario tests knowledge of Mass Assignment vulnerabilities in modern web frameworks.
explanation.why_correct: Mass Assignment occurs when modern MVC or ORM frameworks automatically bind incoming HTTP request parameters to internal model fields without an explicit allowlist (like strong parameters or DTOs), allowing attackers to overwrite sensitive internal properties (e.g., `is_admin`, `balance`).

options_breakdown.Mass Assignment (Over-Posting / Auto-Bin: Correct. Mass assignment automatically binds untrusted input fields to internal model attributes, elevating privileges.
options_breakdown.SQL Injection: Incorrect. The ORM executed valid queries; the flaw was unvetted parameter binding.
options_breakdown.Cross-Site Scripting: Incorrect. XSS executes in client browsers; this altered backend user model permissions.
options_breakdown.XML External Entity (XXE): Incorrect. The payload was JSON, not XML.

explanation.key_term: Mass Assignment: A vulnerability where an active record pattern or object-relational mapping blindly maps user-controlled input into object properties.

questions.question: Which of the following are recognized categories in the authoritative OWASP Top 10 web application security framework? (Select all that apply)
options: Broken Access Control (A01)
Cryptographic Failures (A02)
Injection (A03, including SQLi and XSS)
Overheating CPU Fans (A10)

explanation.asking: This question asks you to identify official OWASP Top 10 risk categories.
explanation.why_correct: Broken Access Control, Cryptographic Failures, and Injection are leading categories in the OWASP Top 10. Hardware fan cooling issues are physical maintenance items, not application security vulnerabilities.

options_breakdown.Broken Access Control (A01): Correct. Broken Access Control is the #1 ranked vulnerability in the OWASP Top 10.
options_breakdown.Cryptographic Failures (A02): Correct. Cryptographic Failures addresses sensitive data exposure and weak encryption.
options_breakdown.Injection (A03, including SQLi and XSS): Correct. Injection covers SQL, command, and cross-site scripting vulnerabilities.
options_breakdown.Overheating CPU Fans (A10): Incorrect. Hardware thermal issues are not web application software vulnerabilities.

explanation.key_term: OWASP Top 10 Categories: Standardized classification of the most prevalent and impactful software security vulnerabilities in modern web applications.
